# The two fields that differ between two runs over one tree, which the golden comparison replaces on
# both sides.
.dist/export/manifest.json :: "commit": null
.dist/export/manifest.json :: "generatedAt":

# Two sources for one consumed corpus: the one this corpus named, and the one that corpus had named in
# turn. Each keeps its own commit, because a record is read where its own producer published it.
.dist/export/manifest.json :: "shortcode": "eng"
.dist/export/manifest.json :: "shortcode": "gp"
.dist/export/manifest.json :: "ref": "1111111111111111111111111111111111111111"
.dist/export/manifest.json :: "ref": "2222222222222222222222222222222222222222"

# This corpus publishes nowhere, and what it inherited still carries the addresses its producers built.
# A merge borrowing this corpus's own template for an inherited record would address a repository that
# holds no such file.
.dist/export/manifest.json :: "target": "none"
.dist/export/glossary/eng/gls-shared.json :: "human": "https://github.com/example/upstream

# One entry per type, counting what this corpus wrote and what it inherited as one number. A consumer
# asks how much of a type there is; which corpus wrote a record is a fact about the line.
.dist/export/manifest.json :: "type": "glossary"
.dist/export/manifest.json :: "records": 2
.dist/export/manifest.json :: "parts": 3

# A type this corpus never adopted, arriving whole because a record here may cite into it.
.dist/export/manifest.json :: "type": "policies"
.dist/export/policies/clauses.jsonl :: "id":"eng:pol-KEEP.HOLD"

# A bare id is this corpus's own, and carries no shortcode. That is the rule a citation already follows,
# so a consumer tells its own records from the rest without being told which corpus it is.
.dist/export/glossary/terms.jsonl :: "id":"gls-local.shelf","title":"Shelf"
.dist/export/glossary/terms.jsonl :: "record":"gls-local","part":"shelf"

# An inherited line names its producer on all three keys that hold an id. `seeAlso` left bare would point
# at whatever this corpus happens to call the same thing, which resolves and resolves wrongly.
.dist/export/glossary/terms.jsonl :: "id":"eng:gls-shared.record"
.dist/export/glossary/terms.jsonl :: "record":"eng:gls-shared"
.dist/export/glossary/terms.jsonl :: "seeAlso":["eng:gls-shared.store"]
.dist/export/glossary/terms.jsonl :: "anchor":"record","shortcode":"eng"

# A grandparent is labelled once. This line arrived inside eng's export already naming `gp`, and keeps
# that name on both keys and on the line. Restamping it would file the record under the corpus this one
# fetched it through and send every link for it to the wrong repository.
.dist/export/glossary/terms.jsonl :: "id":"gp:gls-old.store"
.dist/export/glossary/terms.jsonl :: "record":"gp:gls-old"
.dist/export/glossary/terms.jsonl :: "anchor":"store","shortcode":"gp"
